correctness.rationale: For T=W_{a,b} with T³=0, the standard positive-real Herglotz criterion reduces unitary ρ-dilation of T/t to positivity of the Hermitian Laurent polynomial ρI+zT/t+conj(z)T*/t+z²T²/t²+conj(z)²(T*)²/t², phase-conjugate to a single real symmetric 3×3 H with entries ρ,a/t,b/t,ab/t². Direct determinant expansion gives detH=ρ³−ρ(a²+b²)u+(2−ρ)a²b²u², u=t^{-2}. At first positive determinant/2×2 boundary its exact scale is 1/ρ times sqrt of top eigenvalue L of [[a²,(ρ−1)ab],[(ρ−1)ab,b²]]. Its principal minors remain nonnegative because L≥max(a²,b²) and L≥ρab; immediately smaller t fails PSD. Writing s=a²+b² and p=ab gives L=(s+sqrt(s²−4ρ(2−ρ)p²))/2, strictly decreasing in p for 0<ρ<2 and increasing for ρ>2, constant for ρ=2. Hence balanced and one-zero-edge optimizers exchange exactly at ρ=2, including complex phases via diagonal unitary. Independent symbolic determinant and 30 independent PSD boundary trials corroborate the analytic proof; rank-one and ρ=1 and ρ=2 benchmark cases checked.
